application_targets.label: SATISFIED
application_targets.exact_quote:
The tenancy in question started on 1st January, 1962.
The landlord had produced on the record one statement made by the appellant herein, Jagan Nath before the Income Tax officer, photostat copy of which is Exhibit A.W. 3/1 on the record which indicated that Jagan Nath who was the proprietor of the Bindra Tent House sold the same for Rs.18,000 on 1.1.1970 to his sons Baldev Raj and Sat Pal and he got cash of Rs.8,000 and he gifted the other amount into two equal shares to his sons Baldev Raj and Sat Pal.
application_targets.reason: The target opinion places both the tenancy and the alleged transfer-related conduct well after 9 June 1952. Timing was not the contested basis on which the Supreme Court rejected the eviction ground.
application_targets.uncertainty: LOW: the chronology is express, although the timing element was not separately analyzed.

application_targets.label: DEFEATED
application_targets.exact_quote: There is also no evidence that there has been any subletting or assignment.
application_targets.reason: The target court expressly states that there was no evidence of subletting. This is a failure of evidentiary support, not an affirmative factual finding that every conceivable subletting fact was false.

application_targets.label: DEFEATED
application_targets.exact_quote: There is also no evidence that there has been any subletting or assignment.
application_targets.reason: The target court expressly states that there was no evidence of assignment. The basis is evidentiary insufficiency rather than a factual falsehood.

application_targets.label: DEFEATED
application_targets.exact_quote:
Even though the father had retired from the business and the sons had been looking after the business, in the facts of this case, it cannot be said that the father had divested himself of the legal right to be in possession.
But this is no ground to disentitle him to the benefit of the law if the facts have been proved that he had not parted with possession.
application_targets.reason: The Supreme Court made its own merits application of the retained-legal-possession test and found no divestment or parting with possession.

application_targets.label: SATISFIED
application_targets.exact_quote: There is no dispute that there was no consent in writing of the landlord in this case.
application_targets.reason: The exact negative condition is expressly undisputed: written landlord consent was absent. Its satisfaction does not overcome the failure of all three statutory routes.

application_targets.label: DEFEATED
application_targets.exact_quote:
user by other person is not parting with possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself, or in other words there 330 must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession.
Even though the father had retired from the business and the sons had been looking after the business, in the facts of this case, it cannot be said that the father had divested himself of the legal right to be in possession.
application_targets.reason: The target court applied the qualification itself and found the required parting with legal possession absent because the tenant retained the legal right to possession.

issue_target.label: NOT_SUPPORTED
issue_target.exact_quote:
There is also no evidence that there has been any subletting or assignment.
Even though the father had retired from the business and the sons had been looking after the business, in the facts of this case, it cannot be said that the father had divested himself of the legal right to be in possession.
The eviction order is accordingly set aside.
issue_target.reason: The Supreme Court rejected subletting and assignment for want of evidence and rejected parting with possession on the merits because the tenant retained the legal right to possession; it therefore set aside the eviction order.
issue_target.procedural_limit: This is a merits determination of the fixed section 14(1)(b) ground in the target appeal. The later Article 136 rent enhancement and reservation of other eviction grounds do not alter this fixed-issue result.

Target court states the retained-legal-possession test for parting with possession.
Target court applies the test and finds no divestment of the legal right to possession.
Target court states that the facts proved no parting with possession.
